title: Backtracking
objective: Try a choice, explore it, undo it, and try the other choice, pruning paths that cannot work.

sources.title: Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest and Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, 4th ed. (MIT Press, 2022): recursion

simplifies: All numbers are positive here, which is what makes "the total went over" a safe reason to stop. With negative numbers, that pruning would be wrong.

quiz.prompt: Why undo the choice (pick.pop()) after exploring it?

options.text: So the next branch starts from the same state, without that number
options.explanation: Right. Choose, explore, undo: every branch sees a clean starting point.
It keeps the state correct for the next branch; memory is a side effect.
Python doesn't care; the algorithm does.

quiz.prompt: Why is it safe to stop as soon as the total goes over the target?

options.text: All numbers are positive, so adding more can only make it bigger
options.explanation: Right. That is the pruning, and it relies on positive numbers.
Size doesn't matter; the sign of the numbers does.

options.text: It isn't safe; it can miss answers
options.explanation: With positive numbers it can't: an over-target path can never come back down.
